patch_description: The current best program (273 makespan) uses randomized greedy restarts (6 samples, 0.95 rate) followed by deep local search. The recommendation is to tune the greedy exploration parameters per restart. I keep the winning true-cost greedy + swap/reinsertion local search, but: (1) add a cost cache keyed on tuple sequences to avoid recomputing identical candidates, (2) schedule `sample_rate` from 0.95 down to 0.85 and `num_samples` from 6 up to 10 across restarts — early restarts exploit the greedy signal (confirmed productive at 0.95/6), later restarts diversify, (3) keep the top-3 greedy seeds and run the expensive deep local search on the best one, and (4) run greedy restarts under an overall time budget so no time is wasted. This is a low-risk parameter mutation on top of the proven structure, which should find at least as good a local optimum and likely better ones through diversified late restarts.
